findings: On untouched boxes both readers are near perfect, as long as the lookup and the test use the same RF mode. Silion: locator 32/32, phase pattern 31/32. R700 with mode 2 for both: 32/32 and 31/32. The R700 with a mode 1002 lookup and a mode 2 test drops to 28/32 (phase 21/32), so the lookup has to be captured in the mode that will be used.

Away from calibrated spots the Silion is no better. Called from the other 31 boxes (6" away): Silion locator 18/32, R700 16–18/32. The phase slope does best on both, 20/32 on the Silion and 20–22/32 on the R700.
Methods without a lookup stay near 50% on both readers. Strongest RSSI 13–15/32, firmware vote 14–15/32, WCL with RSSI weights 10–14/32, WCL with slope and RSSI weights 15–21/32.

Most wrong calls are one zone over, across the line the box sits next to. If a box beside a zone line may also be called the zone across that line (655 as Z1 or Z2; the end boxes such as 650 must be exact), the 6" test rises to Silion locator 24/32 and R700 24–26/32, and phase slope to 23/32 and 27–28/32. Strongest RSSI and the firmware vote reach 20–23/32. This is a lenient score: 24 of the 32 boxes sit next to a line.
The Silion's phase is cleaner. Repeated reads on a channel agree to 0.9–1.1°, against 1.6–2.7° on the R700, with no 180° flips. An untouched box's pattern repeats at 0.995 (R700, same mode: 0.989).

12 dBm on antennas 1–2 and 14 dBm on 3–4 gave even coverage. Reads per antenna 4,150–5,270 in 120 s, a median 43 channels per box per antenna, and 16 of 128 box–antenna pairs under 6 channels (R700: 6–31).

At 5 dBm with 3" gaps each port has its own zone. Port 1 reads only zone 1 and port 2 only zone 4; port 3 favours zone 3 (47% of its reads) and port 4 zone 2 (49%). But only 16 of 32 boxes are read at all, and port 1 reads just 2 boxes, so this is the edge of reading, not a working setup.

At 8–10 dBm the beams overlap. Port 1 covers the left half, port 3 the right three zones, port 2 both ends and port 4 everything. 63–88% of the boxes read are seen on 2 or more ports. The 3" gaps changed nothing measurable at 10 dBm.
At 15 dBm every port reads 28–30 boxes across all four zones (30 of 31 boxes on 2+ ports): the beams no longer separate the zones.

The strongest port names the right zone for at most about half the boxes. Taking the 5 dBm beam map (P1→Z1, P4→Z2, P3→Z3, P2→Z4) for every run: 8 and 7 of 32 with 1" gaps at 8 and 10 dBm; 12, 11 and 17 of 32 with 3" gaps at 5, 10 and 15 dBm (at 5 dBm, 12 of the 16 boxes read). One antenna per zone gave 13–15 of 32.
The order along the shelf is P1, P4, P3, P2. The design angles (P3 41°, P1 76°, P4 105°, P2 139°) give P3, P1, P4, P2, so ports 1 and 3 look swapped, at the reader or at the Butler matrix.

Back metal v2 (array mounted on the plate, elements 18 cm apart) is the best Zircon setup. The strongest port names the right zone for 23, 22 and 24 of 32 boxes at 5, 10 and 15 dBm, every box is read, and every zone gets at least 4 right. At 5 dBm only 56% of boxes are seen on 2+ ports and 73% of port 2's reads land in zone 4.
Mounting the array on the plate at 18 cm changed the port order to P1, P4, P3, P2, the same as the Silion. Without metal and with v1 (16 cm, plate only behind it) it was A2, A3, A4, A1.

Stacking the boxes (v3, same antenna as v2) lost zone 4. Ports 3 and 4 stay tight (76% of port 3's reads at 5 dBm in zone 3), but only 2–3 of 8 zone-4 boxes are called right: 19, 20 and 20 of 32, with 4 boxes unread at 5 dBm. Box positions are drawn on the one-layer grid.
A plate held perpendicular to the shelf behind the array (v1) helped zones 1–3 but not zone 4: 19, 19 and 20 of 32, with zone 4 at 2 of 8 because port 4 spills into it and beats port 1.
Without back metal the beams barely separate: 81–96% of boxes are seen on 2+ ports and the strongest port is right for 13, 19 and 16 of 32.
The Zircon reports about 5 dB lower RSSI than the Silion (−48.5 to −52.7 dBm mean against −42.7 to −46.0). Its RSSI is raw and goes through the RF switch, so compare RSSI within one reader only.
